overview: The button triggers an action or a change of state. It ships six visual variants and three sizes, all built from --uix-* tokens so it re-themes automatically in light and dark. Prefer a real <button> element for actions and an anchor styled as a button only when the target is a navigable URL.
whenToUse: Use `primary` for the single most important action in a view; keep it to one per context.
Use `secondary` or `outline` for supporting actions that sit beside the primary one.
Use `ghost` or `link` for low-emphasis or inline actions where a filled button would be too heavy.
Use `danger` only for destructive actions (delete, remove) and pair it with a confirmation.
do: Give every button a clear, action-first label ("Save changes", not "OK").
Keep exactly one `primary` button per decision point so the eye lands on it.
Use the `loading` state (data-loading) for async actions instead of disabling silently.
Render an actual <button> for actions so it is keyboard- and screen-reader-operable for free.
dont: Don't stack multiple `primary` buttons — competing emphasis reads as no emphasis.
Don't rely on colour alone to signal `danger`; the label must also say what will happen.
Don't use a `link` variant for a real navigation link — use an anchor so it opens in-context.
Don't remove the focus-visible ring; it is the only affordance for keyboard users.
a11yNotes: Renders a native <button>, so Space and Enter activation, focus order, and disabled semantics come from the platform.
The focus-visible ring is a --uix-* token and meets the 3:1 non-text contrast minimum in both themes.
`loading` should be paired with an accessible status (aria-busy or an aria-live region) so the wait is announced.
Icon-only buttons must carry an aria-label; a bare glyph has no accessible name.
